title: Tokenization: From Text to Token IDs
summary: Models do not read characters or words; they read tokens, sub-word pieces chosen by a compression algorithm. This lesson builds byte-pair encoding by hand, measures compression, and shows how tokens drive context limits, cost and some famous model blind spots.
objectives: Explain why models use sub-word tokens rather than characters or whole words
Run byte-pair encoding merges by hand by counting adjacent pairs, and compute the resulting compression ratio
Explain byte-level tokenization and why some languages and scripts cost more tokens than others
Estimate the parameter and compute cost of a vocabulary size choice
Convert words to tokens to dollars for a prompt and output, and spot tokenizer quirks that cause bugs
prerequisites: You should know that a model maps numbers in to probabilities out and is trained with cross-entropy over a vocabulary, from [How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn). No other background is needed.
